title: Ya no: marcar el fin de una situación anterior

sections.content: Ya no (no longer) marks the exact moment a previous state of affairs stopped holding true -- essential for a reading about regions that used to be autonomous, invisible to the census, or beyond the reach of conscription, and no longer are. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Amplias regiones del interior ya no estaban físicamente desconectadas del resto del territorio nacional, gracias al ferrocarril.
items.english: Wide interior regions were no longer physically disconnected from the rest of the national territory, thanks to the railroad.

items.spanish: Muchas comunidades rurales que antes gestionaban sus propios asuntos ya no podían hacerlo sin la intervención de alguna autoridad estatal.
items.english: Many rural communities that used to manage their own affairs could no longer do so without some state authority's involvement.

items.spanish: Poblaciones enteras ya no podían permanecer invisibles para el aparato estadístico del Estado.
items.english: Entire populations could no longer remain invisible to the state's statistical apparatus.

items.spanish: Las regiones más remotas del país ya no podían considerarse, con propiedad, territorios ajenos a la autoridad efectiva del Estado nacional.
items.english: The country's most remote regions could no longer properly be considered territories beyond the national state's effective authority.

sections.content: Ya no typically pairs with the imperfect (ya no estaban, ya no podían) when describing a state that gradually stopped holding, contrasting with a period before it -- the imperfect sets the ongoing background, and ya no marks where that background ends.
